title: Icons for the five things the shell can point at
missing: The game has no icon set at all. Player surfaces label everything in words or fall back to whatever glyph the font supplies, and a pinned item is distinguishable from another pinned item only by reading it.

consumerSite.playerVisibleUse: The pin rail and every link or shortcut that reopens something: a person, a commitment in the player's calendar, a measure before a chamber, a government, or an organization such as a local party chapter.

jurisdiction.reason: These stand for kinds of thing rather than for any particular thing, so they are the same in every jurisdiction and in every save.

whyNeeded: Five is measured, not invented: `ShellRef` in src/presentation/shell-navigation.ts is a closed union of exactly five kinds — person, commitment, measure, government, organization — and that file is explicit that a sixth was deliberately not added because it would have had nothing to resolve to. So the set is complete and will not quietly grow.
requestedBy: art bench and regional scenes thread

notes: Five icons, one per ShellRef kind, and no more: person, commitment, measure, government, organization.

Government and organization are deliberately separate, and the distinction must survive at icon size. The navigation code is emphatic that a city and the government of that city are different things and that blurring them is the first step toward implying where the player lives.
A commitment is a scheduled activity in the player's own calendar, not an obligation to somebody — it should not read as a debt or a promise.
Legible at small size in a dense rail, and readable against both light and dark surfaces, because the shell is used at both.
No party emblems, no donkey, no elephant, no real seal of any government. The game generates its own parties and a borrowed emblem would contradict them.
